beliefs: f is piecewise-linear with two slopes: ~4.69 per unit on the far negative side and ~4.71 per unit on the far positive side, meeting at a kink near x=0 [E1, E2, E3, E7, E8, E9]
The negative-side line is f(x)≈4.69*x+6.0 for x<0, and the positive-side line is f(x)≈4.71*x+3.92 for x>0, so the kink is at (0, 3.92) [E7, E8, E9, E10]
The transition is sharp (a true kink at x=0), not a smooth sigmoid: E10 shows constant slope ~4.71 on each side of 0 [E10]
Near x=0 the two lines differ by a small offset (~2.08) that vanishes as |x| grows, consistent with a kink at x=0 [E5, E7]
The exact kink location may be slightly off from x=0 but is close enough that a kink at 0 fits all data [E8, E10]?
notes: Replaced the smooth Gaussian dip with a two-line piecewise model: negative side slope 4.69 intercept 6.0, positive side slope 4.71 intercept 3.92, kink at x=0. This matches E7/E8/E9/E10 slopes and fixes the far-field values that the Gaussian was distorting.
